subject: Follow-up: region availability vs deployment mode - quick clarifications

Subject: Follow-up: region availability vs deployment mode - quick clarifications

Hi Helga — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap and a couple of clarifying questions so we can scope the right deployment pattern for Novabanc.

Call recap (high level):
- Primary requirement: EU-only data residency for production customer PII and inference inputs/outputs.
- Short-term footprint: deploy in EU (Frankfurt or Ireland) only; APAC expansion is possible in 2027 but not required now.
- Risk tolerance: high for data residency; team prefers no cross-region fallbacks for production traffic.
- Procurement asks: SOC2 report, data processing addendum, and a procurement checklist from our side.

Clarifying questions for you:
1) Is strict EU residency (no cross-region fallback of inference requests or KV cache) a hard requirement for the entire contract, or only for a subset of workloads?
2) Would Novabanc consider Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool in EU) vs Private VPC (customer-managed networking) if we can provide explicit controls around cross-region fallback and key management?

What we will provide next (action items):
- A short fact sheet describing how Redwood Hosted enforces region boundaries and the available "strict residency" account flag (attached).
- Technical note on Dedicated vs Private differences (networking, KMS, audit logs).
- SOC2 + DPA template for procurement.

Proposed next step: 30-min technical follow-up with your infra/security lead — would Tuesday 17th 10:00 CET or Wednesday 18th 14:00 CET work?

Attaching: redwood-eu-hosting-fact-sheet.pdf for your initial read.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0132

--
Redwood Inference — Production-first LLM inference

Hi Laura — thanks for the clear recap. A couple quick answers and one follow-up: 

1) EU-only residency is mandatory for all production inference that touches customer PII. Non-PII test/dev traffic can live elsewhere, but production traffic must remain in-EU with no replication to non-EU regions.
2) We are open to Dedicated capacity if it gives an auditable guarantee that compute and KV caches never leave EU boundaries. Private VPC is preferred if it also supports our KMS and logging requirements, but procurement will push back on on-prem due to maintenance cost.

Two asks from our side: 
- Can you provide an explicit statement that Redwood Hosted EU region will not replicate inference requests, KV cache, or backups to the US or other regions by default or for failover? We need something we can show internal security.
- Please include SOC2/ISO docs and an example DPA for review.

We can do the technical call Tuesday 17th 10:00 CET. I will invite our infra lead and a procurement rep.

Regards,
Helga Müller
Head of Cloud Architecture, Novabanc

Subject: Re: Follow-up: region availability vs deployment mode - quick clarifications

Hi Helga — thanks for confirming the call slot and the residency requirement. I took the action from Karthik and put together the technical clarifications below. Attaching a basic EU architecture diagram and a short SLA comparison table.

Brief security-friendly residency statement (for auditors):
"When a Novabanc account is configured in Redwood's EU region, inference requests, model state (KV cache), and production request logs are processed and stored only on compute resources that are physically provisioned within the designated EU region. By enabling the account-level 'strict residency' flag, automatic cross-region fallback for inference traffic is disabled; telemetry required for account health checks can be routed to EU-based observability endpoints. Backups and archival snapshots remain in-region unless explicitly configured to ship to an external storage endpoint outside the EU."
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (summary):
- Hosted (EU region, strict residency): fastest onboarding, managed control plane; optional strict residency flag disables cross-region fallback; Redwood-managed KMS (can be restricted to EU KMS endpoints).
- Dedicated (EU reserved capacity): reserved GPU pool in EU region, dedicated nodes for Novabanc only; includes enhanced audit logs and SLA for throughput/latency; still Redwood-managed control plane unless combined with Private.
- Private VPC (customer-managed): customer VPC or on-prem; customer controls networking, BYO-KMS/HSM, and full isolation; longer lead time and support contract.

Operational caveats:
- Metrics/usage telemetry: by default aggregated telemetry is collected; EU accounts can be configured to keep telemetry in-region, but some global control-plane metadata (account metadata, billing) is stored in Redwood's control plane (we can provide limited export or contractual terms around it).
- Failover behavior: strict residency disables automatic cross-region fallback. We can enable manual, documented failover procedures for DR in coordination with Novabanc if desired.

Attachments included: eu-region-architecture-diagram.png, sla-diff-table.csv

Next steps I recommend for the call:
1) Confirm the strict residency scope (all prod endpoints or subset).
2) Share a short checklist of compliance artifacts we will send (SOC2/ISO/DPA).
3) Outline ballpark numbers (monthly cost ranges) for Dedicated vs Private; I'll draft estimates and bring them to the next meeting.

If helpful, I'll prepare a 1-page TCO spreadsheet we can send before procurement.

Cheers,
Dylan Brooks
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
